newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: Seoul blue chips seen up on foreign ownership plan.
newsitem.headline: Seoul blue chips seen up on foreign ownership plan.

text.p: Seoul blue chips are expected to rise on Thursday as the expected expansion of foreign stock ownership on May 2 would prompt institutional buying, brokers said.
"Institutions are likely to buy blue chips ahead of the limit expansion in bargain hunting," said Koh Kyong-bae, a broker at Hyundai Securities.
The composite stock index ended 1.03 points higher at 702.42 on Wednesday.
But brokers said financial troubles of the Jinro Group could dampen sentiment.
The foreign stock ownership limit is due to be raised to 23 percent on May 2 from the current 20 percent.
Brokers said buying of blue chips would also be backed by Wednesday's consolidation on the shares.
Financial problems with Jinro were highlighted as the group disclosed a plan to sell some of its assets.
Brokers said rising customer deposits with securities houses would buoy overall sentiment.
